mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about an outcome in a random experiment is correct?

options.A: A single possible result that can occur when a random experiment is performed.
options.B: The set of all possible results of the experiment.
options.C: A collection of outcomes that satisfy a particular condition.
options.D: The probability associated with a particular result.

mcqs.answer: A single possible result that can occur when a random experiment is performed.
mcqs.explanation: An outcome is one specific result that may occur when the experiment is carried out. Option B describes the sample space, C describes an event, and D refers to the probability of an outcome, not the outcome itself.

mcqs.question: A die is rolled once. Which of the following sets correctly represents the sample space for this experiment?
mcqs.explanation: The sample space is the set of all possible outcomes. For a single die, the possible results are the numbers 1 through 6. Options B and C are subsets (events), and D includes an impossible outcome (0).

mcqs.question: Which of the following best distinguishes an event from an outcome in a random experiment?

options.A: An event is a single result, while an outcome is a collection of results that satisfy a condition.
options.B: An outcome is a single possible result, whereas an event is any subset of the sample space, possibly containing one or more outcomes.
options.C: An event and an outcome are synonymous terms describing the same concept.
options.D: An outcome is the probability of a result, while an event is the set of all possible outcomes.

mcqs.answer: An outcome is a single possible result, whereas an event is any subset of the sample space, possibly containing one or more outcomes.
mcqs.explanation: An outcome refers to one specific result. An event can consist of one outcome (elementary) or many outcomes (compound), i.e., any subset of the sample space. The other options mix up definitions.

mcqs.question: When two dice are rolled, consider the events: E1 = {sum of the two dice is 7}, E2 = {first die shows 4}, E3 = {both dice show the same number}. Which statement correctly classifies these events?

options.A: E1 is elementary, E2 and E3 are compound.
options.B: E2 is elementary, E1 and E3 are compound.
options.C: E3 is elementary, E1 and E2 are compound.
options.D: All three events E1, E2, and E3 are compound events.

mcqs.answer: All three events E1, E2, and E3 are compound events.
mcqs.explanation: An elementary event contains exactly one outcome. E1 (sum 7) has six outcomes, E2 (first die 4) has six outcomes, and E3 (both dice equal) also has six outcomes. Hence each is a compound event. Options A‑C incorrectly label an elementary event.

mcqs.question: In probability theory, a random experiment is best described as:

options.A: A process that yields a single deterministic outcome each time it is performed.
options.B: A process for which the outcome cannot be predicted with certainty, and each performance may result in one of several possible outcomes.
options.C: A set of all possible outcomes of a deterministic process.
options.D: A calculation of probabilities for a given set of outcomes.

mcqs.answer: A process for which the outcome cannot be predicted with certainty, and each performance may result in one of several possible outcomes.
mcqs.explanation: A random experiment is one whose result is not predetermined; each trial can produce any of the possible outcomes. Option A describes a deterministic process, C confuses sample space, and D describes probability calculation, not the experiment itself.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes an outcome of a random experiment?

options.A: It is the entire set of all possible results of the experiment.
options.B: It is a single possible result that may occur when the experiment is performed.
options.C: It is a collection of results that satisfy a particular condition.
options.D: It is the numerical probability assigned to a result.

mcqs.answer: It is a single possible result that may occur when the experiment is performed.
mcqs.explanation: An outcome is one specific result that can happen in a trial. Option A is the sample space, C defines an event, and D refers to probability, not the outcome itself.

mcqs.question: The sample space in a random experiment is:

options.A: A single possible result of the experiment.
options.B: A set containing all possible outcomes of the experiment.
options.C: A subset of outcomes that satisfy a given condition.
options.D: The probability distribution over the outcomes.

mcqs.answer: A set containing all possible outcomes of the experiment.
mcqs.explanation: The sample space (often denoted S) comprises every outcome that could possibly occur. Option A is an outcome, C is an event, and D describes a probability model, not the sample space itself.

mcqs.question: In tossing a fair coin twice, let event A be 'at least one head appears'. Which description best defines event A?
mcqs.explanation: 'At least one head' includes all outcomes with one or two heads: HH, HT, and TH. Option B is only both heads, C is no heads, and D excludes the case of two heads.
